candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register subjektov nadzora (Register of supervised entities)
candidates.why_relevant: Single authoritative filterable register of ~372 supervised entities across 14+ categories including banks and savings banks, payment institutions, e-money issuers, account information service providers, payment system operators and exchange dealers. This is the master enumeration of WHO is licensed in Slovenian payments and the natural seed list for every other cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Iterate the category filter query parameter (observed pattern ?q[category]=N) and parse the entity listing HTML; keep per-entity detail pages as child records. No export button observed, so HTML parsing with polite rate limiting.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on regulator terminology, then fetched and read the register landing page
queries_used: Banka Slovenije register plačilnih institucij družb za izdajo elektronskega denarja
bsi.si register plačilnih institucij seznam hibridne plačilne institucije

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register plačilnih institucij (Register of payment institutions)
candidates.why_relevant: Dedicated statutory register (under ZPlaSSIED) of payment institutions licensed by Banka Slovenije, incl. those with waiver/exemption, their agents and branches. Directly names the non-bank PSP population Printec would sell to.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the SL and EN variants of the page; extract the entity list and any linked PDF/attachment; diff snapshots quarterly to detect new licences and revocations.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballing from the supervised-entities register and regulator site structure
queries_used: Slovenia register of payment institutions e-money licence list
bizi.si gvin.com Slovenia company financial data payment institutions database

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register družb za izdajo elektronskega denarja (E-money institutions register)
candidates.why_relevant: Central database of e-money institutions (incl. hybrid EMIs), their representatives in SI and host states, branches in host and third countries, plus entities whose authorisation has lapsed. Captures the fastest-moving licensed segment (e.g. Paywiser) and cross-border passporting footprint.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML scrape of register page + companion 'Družbe za izdajo elektronskega denarja' explanatory page; snapshot and diff.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search
queries_used: Banka Slovenije register plačilnih institucij družb za izdajo elektronskega denarja

candidates.why_relevant: Enumerates foreign EEA payment institutions operating in Slovenia via branch, agent or freedom of services — a population invisible in AJPES because they have no Slovenian filed accounts. Essential to size the true competitive field for acquiring and payment services.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape page and the sibling EEA e-money page; cross-check against EBA EUCLID PIR for completeness.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search

candidates.why_relevant: Periodically republished PDF listing notifications received from home-state competent authorities for payment institutions serving Slovenia. Dated filenames make it a good longitudinal series for tracking inbound market entry.

candidates.source_name: AJPES – ePRS, Poslovni register Slovenije (Slovenian Business Register search)
candidates.why_relevant: Central public database of every business entity registered in Slovenia, freely accessible since 17 Oct 2014. Lets you resolve a licensed PSP name to matricna stevilka (registration no.), tax no., NACE/SKD activity, address, representatives and owners — the join key between the BS licence registers and filed financial statements. Also allows SKD-activity sweeps to find ATM/POS servicing companies that hold no payment licence.
candidates.access_status: open (form-driven search; person search requires identifying combinations)
candidates.legal_status: public register, reuse governed by AJPES terms
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the OPSI bulk CSV for the base entity list; use the ePRS web form only for targeted lookups of named PSPs. Respect AJPES reuse conditions and rate limits.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on register terminology
queries_used: AJPES ePRS poslovni register Slovenije iskalnik javni dostop
AJPES iskalnik poslovni register bankomati POS terminali

candidates.source_name: OPSI – Poslovni register Slovenije open dataset (bulk CSV)
candidates.why_relevant: AJPES publishes the PRS unit list (registration number, full name, business address, legal form, registering body, HSMID address id) as free-reuse CSV refreshed twice monthly on the national open data portal. This is the machine-readable backbone for building and maintaining the Slovenian actor map without scraping ePRS.
candidates.legal_status: open data, free reuse under portal licence
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled CSV download via the dataset resource endpoint every two weeks; store versioned snapshots and diff for new/removed entities.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search then snowball to the open-data portal
queries_used: AJPES ePRS poslovni register Slovenije iskalnik javni dostop

candidates.source_name: AJPES – JOLP, Javna objava letnih poročil (public disclosure of annual reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Free access to filed annual reports of companies (including banks, savings banks, insurers and cooperatives) and sole traders: balance sheet and P&L in structured spreadsheet form plus scanned/PDF notes. For PSPs, ATM deployers and POS/terminal integrators these filings are the only public revenue, headcount, asset and margin proxies — directly enabling market sizing per actor.
candidates.access_status: free but registration required; daily quota of 20 business subjects per username (higher volumes by arrangement with info@ajpes.si)
candidates.legal_status: public disclosure mandated by ZGD-1; AJPES reuse terms apply
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Register an account; pull structured statements for a curated shortlist of licensed PSPs and ATM/POS operators, staying inside the 20-subject daily cap or requesting an uplift. Annual cycle: filings for year N publish in the following August (2025 reports published 05.08.2026).
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search plus reading the JOLP help documentation description
queries_used: AJPES letno poročilo plačilna institucija Slovenija javna objava
AJPES JOLP javna objava letnih poročil iskalnik jolp/default.asp

candidates.why_relevant: Publishes every court-register entry (Srg), founding document and change of capital, ownership, name or representatives, with underlying documents published since 1 Feb 2008 and accessible for one year. candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic (weekly) polling filtered to the watchlist of payments entities and to relevant SKD codes; archive documents promptly given the one-year retention window.

negative_findings.description: Searched in both Slovenian and English for a register or licence list specific to ATM deployers or POS terminal operators in Slovenia (bankomati, neodvisni upravljavec bankomatov, POS terminali, upravljavec bankomatske mreže).
negative_findings.result_summary: No Slovenian register of ATM deployers or POS/terminal operators was found. Banka Slovenije registers cover licensed PSPs, EMIs, AISPs and payment system operators, but independent ATM deployment and terminal servicing are not separately licensed or enumerated. These actors are only discoverable indirectly, via SKD-activity sweeps in the AJPES business register plus press and self-disclosure.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's promise to enumerate 'independent ATM deployers and card acquirers' cannot be met from a single register; it requires a constructed list, so downstream cells must not assume the register lists are exhaustive of the ATM/POS landscape.

negative_findings.description: Read the Banka Slovenije 'Register subjektov nadzora' page looking for CSV/XLSX/API export of the ~372 supervised entities across its 14+ categories.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only a searchable/filterable HTML directory was observed; no export control or documented API was visible on the page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection of the authoritative national licence list will require HTML parsing with category-parameter iteration and change-diffing, which is more brittle and needs monitoring for site redesigns.

negative_findings.description: Checked whether the AJPES beneficial ownership register (RDL/eRDL) remains publicly searchable for ownership mapping of small PSPs and ATM/POS firms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple Slovenian sources report that from 09.08.2025 access was substantially narrowed following ZPPDFT-1 amendments, restricting the circle of permitted accessors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ownership mapping must fall back to ePRS founder/partner data and court-register filings; planning a collection routine around RDL would be legally unsound.

negative_findings.description: Assessed whether AJPES JOLP can support bulk harvesting of PSP financial statements.
negative_findings.result_summary: JOLP documentation states free registration is required and imposes a daily limit of 20 business subjects per username, with larger volumes to be arranged via info@ajpes.si.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any plan to sweep hundreds of entities' accounts must either be spread over weeks, negotiated with AJPES, or restricted to a curated shortlist. This should be decided before the collection phase starts.

negative_findings.description: Root URLs for the commercial aggregators bizi.si and gvin.com were inferred from their service names; search results described the services and their pricing but did not return the homepage URLs directly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Service existence, data scope and pricing tiers are attested by search results; the exact entry URLs were not confirmed by a fetch and are recorded as unverified hypotheses.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The downstream verification pass should treat these two URLs as low-confidence and re-resolve them rather than marking the sources dead if they fail.

coverage_gaps.description: No SKD/NACE activity-code sweep was performed to build the candidate list of Slovenian ATM servicing, POS terminal supply and payment-technology companies from the business register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define the relevant SKD codes (e.g. 62.0x IT services, 33.12/33.20 repair and installation of machinery, 46.51/46.66 wholesale of computers and other office machinery, 66.19 other auxiliary financial activities) and run them against the OPSI PRS bulk CSV to generate a candidate actor list, then triage by name and filed accounts.

coverage_gaps.description: Card acquiring in Slovenia is largely performed by banks and by the domestic processor, so no acquirer-specific list was located; scheme-side sources (Visa/Mastercard licensed acquirer and principal-member lists for SI) were not searched in this slice.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted pass on card scheme licensee/principal member listings and on Banka Slovenije card statistics publications to enumerate acquirers, then reconcile against the credit-institution register.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact machine-readable interfaces for AJPES (ePRS reuse service, OPSI resource endpoints) and for EBA EUCLID were not read in detail; only their existence and general terms were established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the AJPES 'Ponovna uporaba' page and the OPSI resource metadata to capture download URLs, refresh cadence and licence text; confirm the EUCLID public API endpoint and its rate limits before designing the pipeline.

coverage_gaps.description: JOLP is described as giving access to recent years online, with older years obtainable only at AJPES offices; the precise online retention window was not confirmed, and eObjave documents are retained online for only one year.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm the JOLP online retention window and start archiving eObjave documents immediately for watchlist entities, since the one-year window means history is irrecoverably lost if collection starts late.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian-language coverage was strong for AJPES and Banka Slovenije, but no Slovenian-language terms were available or used for the supranational EBA/EUCLID sources, which are English-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Accept English-only for EU-level registers; no Slovenian equivalent exists. Continue prioritising SL terminology for all national sources.

brief: Slovenia's register landscape for payments is unusually clean at the licensed end and unusually thin at the hardware end. Banka Slovenije operates a single filterable Register subjektov nadzora covering roughly 372 entities across 14+ supervisory categories — banks, payment institutions, e-money issuers, AISPs, payment system operators, exchange dealers — backed by dedicated PI and EMI registers, EEA passporting lists and dated notification PDFs; AJPES then supplies the identity and money layer via the freely reusable Poslovni register Slovenije (bulk CSV on the OPSI open-data portal), the eObjave court-register gazette for corporate events, and JOLP for filed annual accounts including banks and insurers. Together these turn the licensed market into a named, joinable list with revenue proxies per actor, with EBA EUCLID as an independent cross-check. The material gap is that independent ATM deployers and POS/terminal operators are not licensed or registered anywhere as such, so that population must be constructed by SKD-activity sweeps over the business register and snowballed from press and company self-disclosure; two practical constraints to plan around are JOLP's 20-subjects-per-day cap and the one-year online retention of eObjave documents.
